# Decision log — stage two

Every modelling, scope or process decision, dated, with its reason and the evidence it rests on. Newest last.

> **Entries in this file are never edited after the fact.** A reversal is a **new entry** that cites the old one
> by number. Do not delete a line, do not fix a number in place, do not reword a reason once it is written — the
> value of the log is that it records what was believed at the time. If an entry is wrong, say so in a new entry.
>
> Append with `/decide <text>`, which numbers and dates the entry for you. A hook warns on any edit to this file
> that removes or changes an existing line.

Stage-one decisions are cited as **propsim D-xx** and live in [`vendor/propsim/DECISIONS.md`](vendor/propsim/DECISIONS.md).

| # | Date | Decision | Reason / evidence |

Its engine is **imported, never edited**; an engine change is made as an adapter or subclass in `propedge/`, not in the vendored tree. | D-08 | 2026-09-21 | In the campaign model, **fees are only paid from money the campaign has**: a pass that cannot afford its activation fee is *forfeited*, a running Combine that cannot afford its next subscription is *abandoned*, and both are counted and reported. Subscriptions are billed at the **start** of a day, before anything resolves. By default the campaign **stops buying Combines while a pass is already waiting** for a funded slot (`stop_buying_when_queued=True`) | Letting cash go negative would model an overdraft nobody has and would understate ruin — the quantity the charter requires beside every growth figure. The buying rule was found by a test: past the cap, each further pass buys nothing but $49 + $149 of fees, which over a few hundred days dwarfed the payouts and made every protocol look worse for a reason unrelated to the strategy. The opposite policy remains available as a parameter |
| D-09 | 2026-09-21 | **The spacing of second-and-later payouts is a model assumption**, selected by `PayoutSchedule` (EVEN / EARLIEST / LATEST) and recorded in every result's provenance. | D-10 | 2026-09-21 | **Per-attempt IRR is reported as undefined, with a reason, when it exceeds the solver bracket** — never clipped to the bracket edge. `portfolio_irr` and the reinvestment simulation are the aggregate measures | A few hundred dollars of fees returning thousands a few weeks later annualises to a rate in the tens of millions of percent: arithmetically correct and economically meaningless, since it assumes the cycle repeats instantaneously at a scale the account cap and the calendar forbid. Clipping would invite ranking protocols by an artefact of the bracket. Found by a test whose premise was that lag lowers IRR — both schedules were in fact unsolvable, which is itself the finding (`tests/test_irr.py`) |
| D-11 | 2026-09-21 | The bootstrap for the edge's lower bound resamples **days**, and the reported `lower_bound` is the **more conservative** of the bootstrap and normal-approximation bounds | Trades within a day share a regime and a volatility state, so the day is the independent unit; resampling trades understates the spread and inflates the bound in the optimistic direction — the direction that pushes a candidate over a criterion it should not clear. `tests/test_metrics.py` demonstrates the widening on a log with a shared daily shock **and** its absence when trades are independent, so the test cannot pass for the wrong reason. Taking the more favourable of two methods after seeing both would be choosing a result (cf. D-04) |

| D-13 | 2026-09-22 | **Multiplicity plan.** A pre-registration states **`k` in advance**. Selection happens on a **development period only**; the single selected variant is tested **once** on a **held-out confirmation period** never used in development, and the criterion (e ≥ 0.10, one-sided 95 % lower bound ≥ 0.05) is applied to **that confirmation result only**. With no held-out period, **Bonferroni at one-sided 0.05/k**. An unadjusted bound on a selected variant is **exploratory**. *Decided in session on 2026-09-21, before this log existed; the session numbering (D-05) collided with this file's and is superseded by this number* | Selecting the best of `k` variants and reporting its unadjusted one-sided bound inflates the pass rate by roughly `k`, so an edge that clears the criterion that way has not been demonstrated. Enforced, not encouraged: `propedge.backtest.metrics.criterion_test(..., k=…, has_confirmation_period=…)` applies the level the plan implies and carries the unadjusted estimate separately, labelled exploratory and never used for the verdict; `propedge.backtest.prereg.validate_prereg` refuses a pre-registration that does not declare `k`, the two periods, or the Bonferroni level when there is no held-out period, and the prereg-gatekeeper agent must run it and defer to it. `tests/test_multiplicity.py` includes the case that matters — a bound that clears 0.05 unadjusted and fails at 0.05/20. Amends `CHARTER.md` §"The research criterion" |
| D-14 | 2026-09-22 | **Primary metric.** The primary ranking metric for protocol comparisons is the **median log growth rate of the fee bankroll** in the reinvestment simulation, stated **per horizon and per starting bankroll**. Per-attempt IRR is a **secondary diagnostic**, reported only where uniquely defined (cf. D-10); portfolio IRR likewise. Ruin probability, bankroll drawdown and payout latency are reported beside it. This **supersedes the IRR-first wording of D-02 without editing it**, and amends `CHARTER.md` §Objective — this entry is the citing entry the charter requires. *Decided in session on 2026-09-21; the session numbering (D-07) collided with this file's and is superseded by this number* | Two reasons the ordering changed. A mean over multiplicative outcomes is dominated by its right tail, so mean final cash or annualised growth of the mean multiple can rank a protocol that wipes out most of its paths above one that compounds reliably; `tests/test_primary_metric.py` constructs exactly that disagreement and the ranking follows the median. And per-attempt IRR is structurally unusable as a ranking key here (D-10): a few hundred dollars of fees returning thousands weeks later annualises to a rate that is arithmetically correct and economically meaningless. The reinvestment simulation can carry a ranking because it has to spend the cash on something. `CampaignSummary.median_log_growth` is the headline field, mean-based fields are kept and labelled secondary, a wiped-out path scores `-inf` rather than a clamped floor, and `rank_protocols` sorts on nothing else and refuses summaries that differ in horizon or bankroll |
| D-15 | 2026-09-22 | **Sample size.** Every pre-registration states its **assumed per-trade sd in units of intended risk, and that sd's source**. Stage one's 1.23–1.79 is the **frictionless binary floor** and may not be borrowed. `CHARTER.md` §"The research criterion" is amended to carry the lower-bound caveat now in `docs/HUMAN_INPUTS.md`. *Decided in session on 2026-09-21; the session numbering (D-08) collided with this file's and is superseded by this number* | Stage one's published 1,667 / 2,263 / 3,453 trades are a **floor, not the requirement**, and all three simplifications move it up: the sd is that of a clean two-outcome bracket `(1+R)·√(p(1−p))` and a real log is wider (flattened trades, gapped stops, varying realised risk); `z = 1.645` is the single-test value and the requirement scales with `z²`; and trades are counted as independent when the effective unit is the **day** (D-11). `propedge.backtest.metrics.sample_size_required(edge, sd, *, fraction, z, cluster_factor)` now takes all three, with defaults that reproduce stage one's figures exactly so the baseline did not move. A data-sufficiency claim that cites the published figures without stating its sd, its `z` and its clustering is not a claim about this project's data |
| D-16 | 2026-09-22 | **Control-arm budget.** With `reinvest=False` the control arm's budget is the **initial bankroll less fees paid to date**, never current cash. Payouts still arrive and still count in final cash, but they may not fund further Combine purchases | Otherwise the control arm is not a control. The first implementation used `min(cash, initial_bankroll)`, so once payouts topped cash up the arm kept buying — silently reinvesting inside the arm whose whole purpose is to isolate the contribution of reinvestment from the contribution of the edge. Found by a test that expected one attempt on a \$200 bankroll and got 196. `tests/test_reinvest.py::test_reinvestment_off_cannot_spend_payouts` now pins both the attempt count and the fact that payouts still arrive |

It reproduces the engine exactly *because* it mirrors the control flow — including both `break` conditions, which skip draw calls — and therefore consumes the random stream in the same order, and because it imports the engine's own `EPS` rather than redefining it. Any divergence in that control flow silently changes the draws and the two stop agreeing, so the exactness tests are not a nicety: they are the only thing distinguishing a faithful mirror from a plausible-looking reimplementation. This is also the right instrument for a future re-vendoring (D-12): `vendor/propsim/` is pinned by manifest and cannot drift silently, but replacing it with the closed archive could in principle change the engine, and these tests are what would say so |

Now: the "no new files" test excludes nothing, the cache test is parametrised over both kinds, and a further test reads the three shell callers and fails if any invocation lacks the flag. A boundary that is only checked by its outcome is not a boundary |
| D-21 | 2026-09-22 | **T1: the account cap and hold queue are verified (5, wait-for-a-slot) — but two things the campaign model assumes are wrong.** (a) **The activation fee falls due on ACTIVATION, not on passing.** 8284217: activation is trader-initiated from the Trade Report, payment is step 6 ("Complete Payment to Activate"), and at the cap "the button will be greyed out", so a queued trader *cannot* pay. `propedge/campaign/reinvest.py` charges it on `pass_day` in three places (`AttemptOutcome.cash_flows`, the day-loop step 3, and the string "activation charged on pass" printed into every summary) and **must change**. (b) **A Live Funded Account also consumes the cap**: 8284217 — "If you already have 5 active XFAs or a Live Funded Account, the button will be greyed out." The cap is "5 XFAs **or** an LFA"; `max_concurrent_accounts` counts XFAs only. (c) **`hold_expiry_days` is split out and left unverified**: no official page read states any deadline for a pass awaiting a slot. **Code and tests are not changed in this pass** | Verified on official pages, each quote fetched two to three times with differently-worded prompts by the rules-verifier agent and independently spot-checked in the same session. The number and the queue **match** stage one's record and are now officially sourced, so no design change there. The fee-timing error is **pessimistic** — it charges $149 too early for every held pass, understating growth and overstating ruin — so no existing result is invalidated as too good; but it penalises exactly the aggressive protocols that queue most, which is a bias in a **protocol comparison**, and T7 must not run until it is fixed. `passes_forfeited` is worse than mis-timed, it is the wrong model: with no stated activation deadline a pass that cannot afford the fee today **waits** rather than forfeiting, so the counter destroys value the firm's rules do not destroy — and it cannot be modelled correctly either way until `hold_expiry_days` is answered. That dependency is the sharpest open item T1 produced. Recording the absence as an absence, not as "no expiry", is deliberate: the firm expires a comparable offer (Back2Funded) in 7 calendar days, and 8284215's "XFAs with no trading activity for more than 30 days may be closed" may or may not start its clock at passing |
| D-22 | 2026-09-22 | **T1: running one strategy across several accounts is PERMITTED — the campaign model survives.** Verified from 8284215 ("Can I trade across multiple XFAs at once?" — "Yes, up to $750K buying power using a trade copier"), 13747047 ("Yes! You can trade the same markets across different accounts. What's prohibited is holding opposite positions simultaneously…") and the existence of a first-party Trade Copier (14434175). **Account stacking does not reach this**: 10305426 defines it as repeatedly hitting the MLL and switching accounts to fish for a large win — the fail-and-repurchase pattern already forbidden by the conduct guardrails, not concurrent operation of one genuine-edge strategy. Three constraints the repo did not assume and now carries: the Trade Copier's **Lead account must have the lowest Maximum Position Size** of the group; the copier is **unavailable on Live Funded Accounts**; and a **"$750K buying power" ceiling** applies whose term is **not defined on any official page** | This was the T1 gate that could have collapsed the charter's second half, and it did not: `propedge/campaign/` assumed parallel operation was permitted and it is, so no downstream work is invalidated. Recorded as a decision rather than a bare ledger row because it **adds** constraints. The Lead-MPS rule is inert for a homogeneous 5×50K campaign but means a **mixed-size group trades the smallest account's size**, which is not the same as sizing each account independently — anyone extending the model to heterogeneous accounts must honour it. The undefined "$750K buying power" must not be assumed non-binding without saying so. Two further facts worth carrying: the copier "may disconnect automatically at the start of a new trading day" when Scaling-Plan tiers differ, and turning it off mid-trade "will immediately flatten all Follower accounts" — so **5 accounts are not 5 independent realisations of the strategy**; they share a single point of failure that the campaign model treats as absent. Note also that the help centre's single-user cross-account-hedging prohibition is **stricter than** Terms of Use §27, which only forbids acting "in concert with others"; the stricter reading is what this repo encodes, so nobody later relaxes the guardrail by finding the looser wording |
| D-23 | 2026-09-22 | **T1: the Combine position-size cap is verified at 5 mini-equivalents (50 micros at 10:1), but the FUNDED SCALING PLAN — which is the binding constraint — remains unverified, so T1 is not closed by this verification.** 8284197 gives the table ("$50K \| 5 \| 50") and "Micros and minis count at a 10:1 ratio." The scaling-plan article was found (8284223, page-dated 2026-07-16) and its mechanics are quotable, but **its threshold table is an image**, so no number was recorded and `funded_scaling_plan` stays `null` / unverified. **A conflict between two official sources is recorded rather than resolved silently**: topstep.com/blog/new-permitted-products-offered-at-topstep (2026-01-14) says "Each Micro futures contract equals a full contract toward your max position size" — a 10× difference. The help centre is preferred as the rules authority and is six months later, and the blog is not retracted | The Combine cap is **new information**, not a contradiction: stage one did not model contract caps at all, so this *adds* a constraint. The consequential finding is the ordering. The Combine cap is a flat 5 mini-equivalents from the first trade, but a funded account "starts at a $0 balance" on the lowest scaling tier, so **the funded account is tighter than the Combine** — the opposite of the natural assumption — and the funded account is where the campaign's entire return comes from. Consequence for T4/T6: **do not size a candidate off the Combine's 5 lots.** A sizing sanity check at the verified Combine cap already shows the range in play is marginal — at 50 micros, MES expresses at most $625 / $1,250 / $1,875 of risk at a 10 / 20 / 30-tick stop and MNQ at most $250 / $500 / $750, so a $1,000 risk is untradable on MNQ at every stop in that range and on MES below ~20 ticks; on a fresh XFA at the lowest tier it is likely worse. Under the blog's 1:1 reading nothing in that range is tradable on micros at all, and `propedge/execution/instruments.py`'s own docstring example (33 MES contracts for a $500 risk) is legal only under the help-centre reading — the repo has already assumed it, which is now recorded rather than implicit. Separately on the record from the same reads: a strategy that routinely trades at or near the cap is itself a stated trigger for Responsible Trading Program placement ("You max position a majority of your trades", 13620045), which then imposes a $1,000 DLL — so the cap is not the only reason this risk range is questionable, and it collides with the carried conduct guardrail "risk per position well below the maximum" |
| D-24 | 2026-09-22 | **T1 item 4: payout methods, fees and the processing lag are verified — and `payout_lag_days = 0` must stop being the default.** 8284233 gives, per method: Prop-to-Brokerage "No Fee" / "Same day*"; Aeropay "No Topstep fee" / "Instant after approval"; Wise "No Topstep fee" / "1-3 business days"; ACH "$30" / "1-3 business days"; Wire/SWIFT "$30" / "5-10 business days" — plus "Internal approval can take 1-3 business days." **The $30 fee is method-specific and avoidable in the US**, so `payout_fee` is set to 0.0 (the Aeropay baseline) and the `third_party` flag is closed. **Fee and lag are a single joint method choice**: the available pairs are (fee $0, lag ~3) Aeropay and (fee $30, lag ~6) ACH. Do **not** model ($30, 3) or ($0, 6) — neither exists | The page **never states a combined request-to-receipt total**; it gives approval and transfer as two separate stages, so any end-to-end lag is **derived, not quoted**, and every result using one must say so. Slow-end sums: ~3 (Aeropay), ~6 (ACH), ~13 (wire) business days, which map ~1:1 onto the model's trading-day index. The only route to a 0-day lag is Prop-to-Brokerage "Same day", which delivers into a Topstep **Brokerage** account, not a bank — that cash cannot pay a subscription or an activation fee without a further withdrawal of unstated duration, so 0 is strictly optimistic for a reinvestment model. Why this matters beyond bookkeeping: payout policy is first-order (propsim D-45), and the two errors push opposite ways — a flat $30 that is not actually incurred biases the optimum toward **later, larger** payouts, while a 0-day lag biases it toward **earlier** ones. Stage one's frictions runs carried both at once. Any payout-policy conclusion computed at a flat $30 must be re-run at $0 before it is reported |
| D-25 | 2026-09-22 | **T1 item 5: the section-A rules the campaign model consumes are re-verified, and two are wrong in the repo.** (a) **`billing_days` is 30, not 21** — "It Rebills every 30 days from your original sign-up date" (8284121), independently spot-checked; no official page mentions a 21-day cycle. (b) **The activation fee is now path-dependent**: Standard = $49/month + $149 activation + $49 reset; **No-Activation-Fee = $95/month + $0 activation + $95 reset**, chosen at Combine purchase and fixed ("Paths cannot be changed after purchase"). Everything else in the list — profit target, MLL and its lock, consistency 0.55, both payout paths and caps, the 50 %-of-balance limit, the $125 minimum, the 90/10 split, profit-since-last-payout — **re-reads unchanged**. Two source moves recorded: the profit target is no longer stated on 8284197 (now 8284208), and the fee schedule moved to 14289835 | The billing error is not a rounding error under a time-aware objective. A 21-day cycle bills ~17.4 times a year against ~12.2 for a 30-day cycle, so the repo was **over-charging subscription cost by ~43 % per unit of calendar time** — which changes the cost of a long Combine attempt and therefore the answer to "how long should a failing Combine be allowed to run". Anything computed with 21 must be redone.
